content.text: Section 5.2 contains both exit assistance and data/materials return obligations on MSL, with certification in Attachment 6. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: iii) within [*] Days after expiration or termination of this Agreement, MSL shall return to IBM all copies of IBM Product documentation and all copies of any IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media materials containing IBM confidential information of IBM.
input.rationale: The Agreement already carries the substance of this rule, running in our favour. Section 5.2(a)(ii) obliges MSL, on expiry or termination, to "assist in the transfer of MSL responsibilities and Products as described in Attachment 1: Statement Of Work, to IBM or to another party that IBM designates" — open-ended exit assistance with no duration cap, which is better for us than the preferred six-month window. Section 5.2(a)(iii) requires MSL to return all copies of IBM Product documentation and all IBM confidential documents, discs, tapes and other media within a defined post-termination period, and Section 13.2(c) lets us demand immediate return of all confidential information at any time during the term. Attachment 6 Section 3(a) adds a return-plus-written-certification mechanic for MS Software Image master media. Read together these meet the preferred position on the material terms (assistance plus data return within a fixed window), and comfortably exceed the fallback. Two sub-elements fall short of the model language and are noted rather than flagged: the return obligation does not specify a commonly used machine-readable format, and the certification of deletion is limited to Attachment 6 media rather than covering all IBM data on MSL systems. The return period in 5.2(a)(iii) is redacted ([*] Days), so we cannot confirm it is 30 days or less; if that figure proves materially longer than 30 days we would revisit. Neither point is worth reopening the exit bargain, particularly since the assistance obligation is uncapped in our favour.
